title: See it to Place it: Evolving Macro Placements with Vision Language Models
claim: Our method keeps improving solution quality over the fixed budget, while the standalone baseline plateaus early at worse values.
layout: 3 panels in a row, same axes, shaded confidence bands, shared legend
description: Three side-by-side line plots, labeled (a) superblue5, (b) superblue16 and (c) superblue18. Each plots global HPWL (×10^7, lower is better) on the y-axis against number of rollouts, from 0 to 2000, on the x-axis. A blue step curve is the standalone DREAMPlace baseline (DP 4.3.0). An orange step curve is the method (VP+DP 2.5 Flash). Both curves have translucent shaded bands for standard error. The blue curve flattens early, around 300 to 1000 rollouts. The orange curve keeps stepping down and ends lower in all three panels. The gap is small in (b) and largest in (c), where blue stays near 22.3 and orange falls to about 21.5. Each panel has a legend at the top left. The eye goes first to the orange curve diverging below the blue one.
caption: \method-guided DREAMPlace on (a) superblue5, (b) superblue16, and (c) superblue18. VP+DP denotes \method{} with DREAMPlace; DP 4.3.0 is standalone DREAMPlace. We report mean and standard error of the best gHPWL observed ($\times 10^7$, lower is better) across three random seeds with 2,000 rollouts each, using Gemini 2.5 Flash. The continued decrease in gHPWL demonstrates how \method{} improves placement quality over the fixed rollout budget, whereas standalone DREAMPlace converges early.
abstract: We propose using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for macro placement in chip floorplanning, a complex optimization task that has recently shown promising advancements through machine learning methods. Because human designers rely heavily on spatial reasoning to arrange components on the chip canvas, we hypothesize that VLMs with strong spatial reasoning capabilities can effectively complement existing placement algorithms. We introduce VeoPlace (Visual Evolutionary Optimization Placement), a novel framework that uses a VLM, without any fine-tuning, to guide the actions of a base placer by constraining it to subregions of the chip canvas. The VLM proposals are iteratively optimized through an evolutionary search strategy with respect to resulting placement quality. Using global half-perimeter wirelength (gHPWL) after standard-cell placement and legalization as the evaluation metric, VeoPlace boosts ChiPFormer performance on 9 of 10 benchmarks with peak reductions exceeding 32%. We further demonstrate that VeoPlace generalizes to analytical placers, improving DREAMPlace on all 8 evaluated Superblue benchmarks with gains up to 4.4%. Our approach opens new possibilities for electronic design automation tools that leverage foundation models to solve complex physical design problems.
